topics.flagship-ru-ua: Missile attacks wounded 9 people as Ukraine prepares for a fourth round of talks with Russia and the U.S. brokered by the Trump administration; the last round was in Geneva in February. Zelenskyy reportedly says Russia is stepping up attacks ahead of the Tuesday meeting in Abu Dhabi, and a separate report says a single attack killed 50 people in Zaporizhzhia. Other reporting covers British and French preparations of thousands of troops for a possible post-ceasefire peacekeeping mission, and oil traders reportedly shunning Russian diesel.
topics.flagship-ir-il: The Houthis say 22 people were killed in a strike on the village of al-Shariya near Sanaa and blame Saudi Arabia; Riyadh had not initially commented. Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it has lifted its self-imposed limit on ballistic missile range. Single-source reports describe continued US strikes on Iran with Qeshm island and Hormuz hit and mediators trying to prevent escalation, and Iran reportedly distributing iodine pills near nuclear sites as Trump weighs fresh strikes. The reports on the US-Iran situation are not fully consistent.
topics.T15: Catastrophic flooding along the Tennessee-Georgia border, described by forecasters as a once-in-1,000-year event, is moving up the Atlantic coast. A landslide prompted an evacuation order in Zeballos, B.C.; Indonesia reported a military helicopter crash during wildfire response; Mount Bromo in East Java erupted; and a magnitude 4.7 quake off Ecuador triggered no tsunami alert. The Hurricane Helene and Spanish volcano megatsunami items appear to be older or generic content rather than new events.
topics.T01: Dozens of flights across Europe were targeted by hoax bomb threats this week, causing diversions and emergency landings. China confirmed for the first time that it is discussing a possible Xi-Trump-Putin meeting. The Cameroon Anglophone conflict and Sudan items are retrospective or generic and add little new; the Yemen strike is covered under Iran / Israel / Middle East.
topics.T02: Storm rains flooded tents of thousands of displaced families in Gaza, with Civil Defence reporting 1,500 distress calls in 10 hours. The UN warns that fewer than 1 million of the 15.4 million people in Sudan who need emergency shelter have received assistance as funding runs low. Reports also cite rising child malnutrition in Sudan.
topics.T03: The White House science office announced it will begin screening purchases of synthetic nucleic acids to reduce the risk of AI-enabled bioweapons. Quebec provincial police confirmed that a US Army barrel found on an island in the St. Lawrence River does not contain active anthrax, though the origin remains a mystery.
topics.T04: Arizona confirmed its fifth New World screwworm case, in a dog near Thatcher, and expanded its quarantine into Graham County. About 800 cow carcasses were reportedly burned near Moscow after a lumpy skin disease outbreak at a farm, per Telegram channels. Sokoto State and UNICEF are promoting a polio vaccination campaign for November 7-11.
topics.T05: Pedro Alliana became president of Paraguay after Santiago Pena was impeached over a banking crisis that left nearly half the country unable to access accounts. Other items are single-source: Polish opposition MPs unfurled a 'TUSK=DICTATOR' banner during a visit by EU Parliament President Metsola, a poll reportedly puts Macron's approval at 13%, and Bangladesh continues prosecutions tied to the July Uprising.
topics.T06: France deployed 70,000 security personnel ahead of fresh nationwide protests over living costs, with unions and student groups mobilizing and a Yellow Vests rally in Paris despite an official ban. Thousands of government workers, teachers and transport staff walked off the job over low wages and living costs. Single-source pieces describing France's 'biggest uprising since 1968' and a Macron bunker are commentary or book-based claims.
topics.T07: No standalone nuclear weapons stories today. The only item, covered under Iran / Israel / Middle East, is a commentary noting a $20 million reward offer for information on Iran's nuclear program.
topics.T08: A gunman firing from a car killed at least six people, including a British tourist, in Krakow's main market square; the suspect was wounded by police and hospitalized. In Congo, an attack by an Islamic State-loyal group reportedly killed at least 44 people and forced patients to flee an Ebola clinic. Other items include a terrorist attack in Amman that killed a Public Security officer, a foiled attack on a Kwara, Nigeria community, a Haitian gang leader killed by police, and bomb threats ahead of Dublin summits.
topics.T10: Reports say Russia's Mi-28NM fired a cruise missile in Ukraine, and Lockheed Martin received a $694 million contract to move the AGM-183A hypersonic missile to production for the B-52. Trump's proposed battleship fleet could cost about $275 billion, per one report, and the incoming Democratic House is expected to push a defense-spending showdown. Defense Secretary Hegseth faces a possible impeachment vote after the midterms, per one report.
topics.T11: Cuba held an Army and Navy exercise that briefly showed drones U.S. intelligence says were bought from Russia and Iran. Other drills include Pakistan-Tajikistan Dosti-III counter-terrorism, India-US Tiger Triumph 2026, India-Myanmar Rahat Mitra, Kuwait's Desert Flash 1, and China-Pakistan Karakoram-2026, which a former Indian Army chief said warrants heightened surveillance.
topics.T12: Italian PM Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers after personal data stolen from Foreign Minister Tajani was published, following a week of bomb threats against EU flights. A health intelligence-sharing group warned members to lock down systems after cyberattacks on cold storage systems, including a French blood bank. Russia's statistics agency Rosstat reportedly lost 23TB of data, including war casualty figures, in a hack.
topics.T14: The Trump administration has reportedly ordered Lebanese diplomat Ibrahim Charara to leave the US over social media posts praising Hezbollah's 1983 Marine barracks bombing, according to a single-outlet report.
topics.T16: Republicans are reeling from a midterm wipeout, with figures such as DeSantis and Cruz using extreme language about the result and questions raised about Trump's grip on the party. Democrats are set to take the House on Jan. 3, with healthcare and ending the Iran war as early priorities. New Zealand's election is undecided, with provisional results showing a nine-seat overhang and 66 seats needed for a majority. Nigerian pre-2027 campaign items include a dispute over alleged attacks on an ADC rally in Kebbi.

bluf: Yemen's Houthis say a strike near Sanaa killed 22 people, accusing Saudi Arabia of hitting homes in al-Shariya; Riyadh had not initially commented. Ukraine is preparing for a fourth round of Trump-brokered talks with Russia and the U.S. as missile attacks wounded 9 people; negotiators are due to meet Tuesday in Abu Dhabi, and Zelenskyy reportedly says Russian attacks are intensifying. A gunman firing from a car killed at least six people, including a British tourist, in Krakow's main market square; the suspect was wounded and hospitalized. Zaporizhzhia is reportedly increasingly dangerous, with one account citing 50 people killed in a single attack. Dozens of European flights have been hit by hoax bomb threats this week, causing diversions and emergency landings; the source and any link between the threats remain unclear. Italy's Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers for publishing data stolen from Foreign Minister Tajani, a cyber incident reported alongside the bomb-threat wave. Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it has lifted its self-imposed limit on ballistic missile range, while single-source reports describe continuing US-Iran strikes and Hormuz ship attacks.
